## p176a — Breakthrough toward the north or northeast

**Edition context:** p176a — Breakthrough toward the north.

<a id="edition-cases-p176a-p176a--breakthrough-toward-the-north"></a>



**Status:** Earlier suggested body is reproducible only with additional plaintext-derived corrections. **Key:** `Nov10-12`.

**Earliest credited record:** [Norbert, 2017-03-02, comment 26](https://scienceblogs.de/klausis-krypto-kolumne/2017/02/23/the-top-50-unsolved-encrypted-messages-46-unsolved-adfgvx-cryptograms-from-world-war-1/?all=1#comment-853025). **Current source and arithmetic review:** icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro, 2 November 2026.

<a id="edition-cases-p176a-most-likely-reading"></a>

### Most likely reading

**Readable German — earlier credited partial reconstruction:**

> [Durchbruch vorbereitet]. [Durchbruchsrichtung] nach Norden oder Nordosten […] kann jetzt noch nicht [beurteilt werden].

**Meaning:** A breakthrough is being prepared. Whether its direction will be north or northeast cannot yet be assessed.

**Notes:** The intended sense follows Norbert's suggested body. A complete grammatical sentence requires editorial intervention; its extra repairs were not fully specified in the original comment. The exact-body certificate documents how to encode that proposal, while the direct reconstructed stream below retains its discrepancies. The current audit does not identify an independently recovered complete sentence.

### Review

- The primary source has 214 literal slots, 204 valid coordinates and 10 erased slots. Its GAVD group is short and the final ADAA- has a printed erasure.

- Among five possible missing-slot positions within the short GAVD group, insertion after G requires 13 additional known-symbol changes plus 7 unknown-slot fills to encode the prior wording; insertion after the whole group, as implied by the legacy filled transcript, requires 16. This comparison is conditioned on the prior wording, not independent recovery.

<a id="edition-cases-p176a-source-retention-bound-for-the-earlier-proposal"></a>

### Source-retention bound for the earlier proposal

Fixing **Norbert's 112-position proposal above**, including `BEEURTEILT`,
and the unchanged Nov10–12 key gives an exact conditional bound. The search
allows added slots anywhere while retaining every observed source coordinate
in order; no five-group location is assumed.

| Alignment family | Added slots | Excluded source | Minimum observed substitutions | Optimal maps |
| --- | ---: | --- | ---: | ---: |
| All 214 source slots | 10 | None | **68** | 252 |
| Exclude final printed mask 213 | 11 | One mask | **13** | 2 |

The first family fills all ten printed masks; the second fills the nine
surviving masks. Every added slot is also filled from the fixed proposal.
Among all ten possible single printed-mask exclusions, **only final mask
213 attains 13**; the other exclusions require at least 30 substitutions.
Thus two missing five-coordinate blocks alone cannot reconcile the complete
literal source with that wording at the prior repair price.

These bounds quantify the proposal's dependence on treating the final dash
as extra. They do not establish that the dash is extraneous or that the
wording is historical. The target uses only known square cells; all 120
injective completions of the missing digits produce the identical encoding.

The [source-retention certificate](../experiments/p176a_source_retention_bound/certificates.json)
contains every optimal insertion map and attaining witnesses. A separate
encoder and suffix dynamic program independently check the forward-program
bounds and exact map counts. [Reproduce the bound](../experiments/p176a_source_retention_bound/README.md).
This additional source and arithmetic audit is by **icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro**;
the earlier wording and all displayed readings above retain their original credit.

## p176 A5 — Messages and material first to Hermannstadt; provisioning fragment

**Edition context:** Romanian ultimatum and the crossing near Rustschuk.

**Related source pages:** [p175 C1](175.md#source-p175-c1), [p175 C2](175.md#source-p175-c2).

<a id="edition-cases-military-romanian-ultimatum-companions-romanian-ultimatum-and-the-crossing-near-rustschuk"></a>



**Source edition: icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro.**

Three newly source-edited parts belong to Childs's six-part message
on printed pp175–176, PDF pages 178–179. The repeated header is
`LP v NKJ (5.40 p.m., November 10th); VON UKS KR 0915 (10/11) 6 TLE`.
Its fourth part is the existing [p176a challenge](#edition-cases-p176a), whose
breakthrough proposal retains prior credit to **Norbert and Max Baertl
in 2017**. This frozen three-record companion edition left two other
surviving parts unread; separate later editions now address C3 and A6.
Those parts remain excluded from its original three-record count.

The message reports that the Romanian government has presented an
ultimatum to evacuate its territory or lay down weapons. It then reports
French troops beginning to cross the Danube near Rustschuk and fighting
in progress. A later part discusses sending messages and material first
to Hermannstadt. These are statements in the intercepted report, not
independent confirmation of the events or their timing.

<a id="edition-cases-military-romanian-ultimatum-companions-surviving-unread-parts-and-the-earlier-challenge"></a>

### Surviving unread parts and the earlier challenge

The source sequence is C1, C2, C3 on p175, followed by A4, A5, A6 on
p176. C3 has **217** printed slots against a stated length of **222**;
the missing five coordinates have no selected location. A6 has **160**
printed slots, of which **86** are dashes. Both are retained as source
context within this frozen companion edition, with no contribution to its
three-record totals. The later [conditional C3 withdrawal edition](175.md#edition-cases-military-p175-c3-withdrawal-followup)
now supplies a readable candidate while preserving all tied loss layouts.
The separate [conditional A6 coal-train fragment](#edition-cases-military-p176-coal-train-fragment) now proposes 48/80 positions through 44 printed-mask fills and no observed-coordinate changes; its routing field and later tail remain raw.

A4 is already cataloged as p176a. Its earlier reconstructed text and
missing-block assumptions remain separate from these native-frame
companions. Being part of the same source-labeled message does not
independently prove the earlier reconstructed letters.

<a id="edition-cases-military-romanian-ultimatum-companions-exact-scope-of-the-edition"></a>

### Exact scope of the edition

The three new records contain **588 printed slots**, **580 observed
coordinates**, and **294 plaintext positions**. Their raw readings fix
**284** positions; the separately recorded candidates fix **291** after
**six known-coordinate substitutions and seven printed-dash fills**.
One printed dash and two occurrences of an unknown key label remain.
There is no modeled gap, deletion or key change in those three records.

Earlier unreviewed screening already contained the readable C2 and A5
bodies; C1 was garbled in a shorter OCR-derived frame. The present
contribution is exact source transcription, the full arithmetic and
uncertainty record, and a transparent assembly with prior credit.
No first historical decipherment claim is made.

The [package](../experiments/romanian_ultimatum_companions/README.md),
[inputs](../experiments/romanian_ultimatum_companions/inputs.json) and
[certificate](../experiments/romanian_ultimatum_companions/certificates.json)
preserve all coordinates, domains, repairs, source crops, unread context,
and complete compatibility witnesses for the unresolved fields.

## p176 A6 — Conditional coal-train continuation via Klausenburg with a repeated-place hypothesis

**Edition context:** p176 A6 — Conditional coal-train continuation via Klausenburg.

<a id="edition-cases-military-p176-coal-train-fragment-p176-a6--conditional-coal-train-continuation-via-klausenburg"></a>



**Partial word proposal and source review: icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro.**
The sixth part permits a coherent continuation about coal trains via
Klausenburg and the phrase “gerechnet werden.” This is a **context-conditioned
partial proposal**, supported by the preceding fifth part and compatible
with every observed sixth-part coordinate. The routing field and later tail
remain unread. No complete historical message or unique wording is claimed.

A [conditional repeated-place supplement](../experiments/p176_repeated_place/README.md)
proposes `XKLAUSENBURGX` in the first omitted field. It adds **eleven fixed
positions**, reaching **59/80**, with **zero observed substitutions and
fifteen additional printed-mask fills**. All 74 observed coordinates remain
unchanged. The two copies are both partly supplied: repeating the earlier
proposed place is a separate hypothesis, not an independently received
complete-word witness.

The native spans force only five shared letters after assuming repetition;
each of the 120 injective square completions still admits **46,656** common
strings. `XBLANKENBURGX` fits the second span at the same price. Four newly
assigned positions have neither coordinate observed. The supplement retains
these limits, the inherited `N`/`X` alternative, and the entirely uncompleted
last 24 positions. The displays below preserve the separately priced earlier
edition; the supplement contains its full conditional stream and exact ledger.

<a id="edition-cases-military-p176-coal-train-fragment-why-propose-these-words"></a>

### Contextual basis for the proposed words

The printed header and consecutive part labels put A5 immediately before A6
in the same six-part message. Its previously edited ending begins
`KANNMITZUFUEHRUNGVON` and ends with the literal conjunction `UND`.
That syntax motivates dative plural `KOHLENZUEGEN` at the start of A6.
The exact native half-coordinate constraints also permit
`UEBERKLAUSENBURG` at positions 12–27 and `GERECHNETWERDEN` at 41–55.
These words are contextual proposals; compatibility does not prove them.

<details>
<summary>Earlier attributed reading</summary>

**Earlier attributed reading — A5 proposal by icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro, reproduced with its unresolved field; not counted as a new record here:**

```text
NACHRICHTENUNDMATERIALZUNAECHSTNACHXHERMANNSTADTXXKANNMITZUFUEHRUNGVONVERPFLEG?ZXUND
```

</details>

That prior A5 reading costs **three observed substitutions** (source
58 G→F, 108 X→D, 120 A→D) and **four printed-mask fills** (51 F, 52 G,
53 D, 54 A). Its `VERPFLEG?Z` field remains unresolved; this edition neither
completes that field nor folds those seven prior changes into A6's price.
The [earlier companion edition](#edition-cases-military-romanian-ultimatum-companions) and the
frozen context snapshot retain its provenance.

The word spans arose during a bounded German word-model exploration followed
by comparison with A5. The highest-scoring complete model output was not
coherent German. No language-model score, dictionary hit or round trip is
treated as proof of historical uniqueness.

<a id="edition-cases-military-p176-coal-train-fragment-alternatives-and-global-uncertainty"></a>

### Alternatives and global uncertainty

At plaintext position **11**, separator `X` is also compatible at the same
price: `KOHLENZUEGEXUEBERKLAUSENBURG`. It replaces the proposed source-mask
151 `D` with `G`, leaving the total at zero observed changes and 44 mask
fills. The dative `N` is preferred only by the A5 context.

The field at **28–40** stays exactly `???A???????G?`. Ordinary place-word
completions can fit its sparse constraints; neither Marienburg nor
Blankenburg is selected. The last 24 positions also remain exactly raw.
Their literal `1` is not assigned a historical date or reference meaning.

Five square cells remain globally unassigned: `FD`, `GF`, `XA`, `XG`, `XX`.
They take distinct values from `{5,6,7,8,9}`. The verifier checks all **120**
injective assignments without selecting any one of them. For each, a
constructed full witness fills the remaining 42 coordinate masks with `A`
and exactly re-encrypts through two column encoders while retaining every
observed source coordinate. Those arbitrary witness fills are **not part of
the edited output** and supply no historical plaintext.

## p176b — Army positions near Peterreve and Versecz

**Edition context:** p176b — Army positions near Peterreve and Versecz.

<a id="edition-cases-p176b-p176b--army-positions-near-peterreve-and-versecz"></a>



**Status:** Earlier 2026 body verified after its published missing 20-coordinate block; three unit-number cells remain unassigned. **Key:** `Nov10-12`.

**Earliest credited record:** [Prinz and GPT-6 Astra, 2026-09-19](https://www.prinzai.com/p/another-wwi-german-radio-cipher-falls). **Current source and arithmetic review:** icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro, 2 November 2026.

<a id="edition-cases-p176b-shared-square-reconstruction"></a>

### Shared-square reconstruction

The [joint Nov10–12 reconstruction](../experiments/nov10_joint_completion/README.md) supports the same formations in the order **219, 217, 6**. It combines the earlier unordered division identifications with the independently attested Romanian mobilization date and the remaining army-number constraint. The earlier **217, 219, 6** order remains the complete alternative when the date association is dropped.

**Conditional interpretation — revised formation order:**

> An O.H.L. 11. Armee: Alpenkorps, Raum Peterreve–Verbasz. [219.], [217.], [6.] R.D.D., Linie Nagybesskerek–Versecz. Versecz von Serben besetzt.

The three digits come from observed pairs in the reconstructed frame; the earlier twenty-coordinate missing block is retained. These positions were already supplied by the attributed historical overlay and are excluded from the joint package’s twenty new positions.

<a id="edition-cases-p176b-earlier-contextual-reading"></a>

### Earlier contextual reading

**Readable German with a conditional historical overlay.** The bracketed units retain the previously published Prinz / GPT-6 Astra interpretation; this review does not relabel them as new unchanged-key output.

> An O.H.L. 11. Armee: Alpenkorps, Raum Peterreve–Verbasz. [217.], [219.], [6.] R.D.D., Linie Nagybesskerek–Versecz. Versecz von Serben besetzt.

**Display notes:** `[217.]` and `[219.]` expand the raw fields `21?`; only the last digit in each is unassigned. `[6.]` supplies the separate raw `?` field. The brackets display historical identifications, not three fully unread unit numbers or a new substitution-square assignment.

**Meaning:** To Supreme Army Command: the 11th Army's Alpine Corps is in the Peterreve–Verbasz area; the indicated divisions are on the Nagybesskerek–Versecz line. Versecz is occupied by Serbian forces.

**Notes:** The three bracketed unit digits are the contextual 217/219/6 interpretation published by Prinz with GPT-6 Astra. Independent unit-history evidence supports that interpretation, but the attested substitution square still leaves those digits unresolved. The missing 20-coordinate block is an explicit reconstruction, not an observed part of the ciphertext.

<a id="edition-cases-p176b-review"></a>

### Review

- The primary header is RICHI-240 and 220 coordinates were received. This independently supports a 20-coordinate shortage, but does not determine the missing symbols.
- The three unit digits use unassigned Nov 10–12 square cells. They cannot be fixed from this ciphertext and the attested key alone.
- The 217/219/6 wording is supported by an independently checked French report dated 19 November describing 11 November forces. That is contextual evidence, distinct from a cryptographic assignment of the missing digits.

<a id="edition-cases-p176b-division-history-review"></a>

### Division-history review

The French report's `6e D.I. reserve` initially appears to conflict with the U.S. divisional history's August dissolution of the 6th Reserve Division. [The reviewed German unit history](../data/reviews/p176b_unit_context.json) continues the designation through its Balkan retreat, while the organizational account describes reuse of the dissolved division's staff. This substantially reconciles the historical designation; it does not fill the unknown cipher-square digits. The [German battle calendar excerpt](../sources/excerpts/ruhmeshalle_6rd_p385.png) and exact source qualifications are retained.

<a id="p176-b2-p176-b3--the-danube-field-report-two-companion-parts-1011-november"></a>

## The Danube field report: two companion parts, 10–11 November

**Sources on this page:** p176 B2, p176 B3.

<a id="edition-cases-military-nov10-danube-field-report-the-danube-field-report-two-companion-parts-1011-november"></a>



**Source edition and exact repair audit: icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro.**

Childs printed p176 B, PDF page 179, labels a three-part message
`LP v ZÖN (3.38 a.m., November 11th); 2305 (10) 3 TLE`.
Its first part is the existing [p176b challenge](#edition-cases-p176b), credited
to **Prinz and GPT-6 Astra, 19 September 2026**. The two parts below
complete the source-labeled sequence; they do not solve the first
part's reconstructed 20-coordinate shortage or unknown unit digits.
Only these two physical records are new catalog entries.

These texts report French forces, a Danube crossing near the literal
place-name `RUSTUK`, and reserves north of `SLOBOZIE`. The edition treats
those statements as the sender's report; it does not independently
establish that the reported movements occurred. The two parts retain
their native source lengths and the unchanged published **Nov10–12**
square and ranks.

<a id="source-p176-b2"></a>

### p176 B2

The [252-coordinate source](../experiments/nov10_delegates_and_field_report/sources/p176_B2.png)
directly reads:

<details>
<summary>Raw decoded text</summary>

**Raw output:**

```text
FEHERTEMPLOMXFOLGENFRANZOSENXXBESATZUNSHEERXFEINDVORFUEHLTEGEGENNEUESTELLUNGENDONAUKNIEXSAMVITXNACHAGENTENSTARKMITENGLAEN?ERNX
```

</details>

A single observed-coordinate replacement gives:

<details>
<summary>Proposed text and exact labels</summary>

**Edited output:**

```text
FEHERTEMPLOMXFOLGENFRANZOSENXXBESATZUNSHEERXFEINDVORFUEHLTEGEGENNEUESTELLUNGENDONAUKNIEXSAMVITXNACHAGENTENSTARKMITENGLAENDERNX
```

</details>

The final word becomes `ENGLAENDERN`, in a report attributed to agents.
The source-derived `BESATZUNSHEER`, unusual order `FEINDVORFUEHLTE`, and
`SAMVIT` remain untouched. No extra letter is inserted into the first
word, no phrase is reordered, and no place-name is silently modernized.

The original question mark is pair `FD`, whose domain is **56789** in
the partial square. Source coordinate **108** changes **F→G**, turning
that pair into a known `D`. This is an explicit ciphertext repair, not
a fill of an erased coordinate or an assignment of an unknown key cell.

<a id="edition-cases-military-nov10-danube-field-report-scope-and-attribution"></a>

### Scope and attribution

These two parts total **524 observed coordinates**, **262 plaintext
positions**, **261 raw fixed labels**, and **262 candidate fixed labels**.
Their cost is **five observed-coordinate substitutions**, with no
coordinate fill, loss model, deletion or key change. All candidate
characters re-encrypt to the exact explicitly repaired streams.

Earlier unreviewed whole-corpus screening already produced readable
bodies for both parts. The contribution here is source transcription,
the complete coordinate and domain ledger, and verification of the
parts' printed relationship. A bounded review of the paper, thesis
and cached comments found no separate explicit discussion of these
two bodies; that absence does not establish historical priority.

The report shares geographical context with the already reviewed
Nov9 operational messages and the Nov3 Mackensen report. It is not
presented as an exact copy of either. The old p176b unit interpretation
also remains an independent conditional layer.
